numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Densifying a datetime64/timedelta64 SparseArray returns an object-dtype array whose stored values are boxed by numpy as datetime.datetime (coarser units) or raw integers (nanoseconds), beside the pandas-boxed fill value, so one array holds two types. Separately, to_dense with an explicit dtype truncates a nanosecond Timestamp/Timedelta fill value to microseconds, and a fill_value in a different unit than the column is read as a raw integer under a numeric cast.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The dense result should match the dense (non-sparse) result: a datetime64/timedelta64 array in the subtype's unit with the fill value converted to that unit, not an object array mixing datetime.datetime or integers with the fill value. A nanosecond Timestamp or Timedelta fill value should not be truncated to microseconds.
trigger_conditions: SparseArray with datetime64 or timedelta64 subtype
fill_value is a pandas Timestamp, Timedelta, or np.nan
dtype is None, as in astype(object) or Series.to_numpy()
to_dense or Series.to_numpy called with an explicit dtype
nanosecond-unit Timestamp or Timedelta used as fill_value (truncated to microseconds by np.full)
fill_value whose unit differs from the column's unit (read as a raw integer under a numeric cast)
Sparse array must contain gaps (ngaps >= 1) so the fill value is actually used

provenance.value: pandas.core.arrays.sparse.array.SparseArray.__array__ and pandas.core.arrays.sparse.array._promote_for_fill (also SparseArray.to_dense and Series.to_numpy on datetime64/timedelta64 SparseArray)

Densifying a datetime64/timedelta64 SparseArray returns an object-dtype array whose stored values are boxed by numpy as datetime.datetime (coarser units) or raw integers (nanoseconds), beside the pandas-boxed fill value, so one array holds two types. Separately, to_dense with an explicit dtype truncates a nanosecond Timestamp/Timedelta fill value to microseconds, and a fill_value in a different unit than the column is read as a raw integer under a numeric cast.

The dense result should match the dense (non-sparse) result: a datetime64/timedelta64 array in the subtype's unit with the fill value converted to that unit, not an object array mixing datetime.datetime or integers with the fill value. A nanosecond Timestamp or Timedelta fill value should not be truncated to microseconds.
